<p id="mwEA"><b id="mwEQ">MOIL</b> (earlier known as <b id="mwEg">Manganese Ore (India) Limited</b>) is a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniratna" title="Miniratna" class="mw-redirect" id="mwEw">miniratna</a> government <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manganese_ore" title="Manganese ore" class="mw-redirect" id="mwFA">manganese ore</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mining" title="Mining" id="mwFQ">mining</a> company headquartered in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagpur" title="Nagpur" id="mwFg">Nagpur</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India" title="India" id="mwFw">India</a>. With a market share of 50%, it is the largest producer of manganese ore in India.<sup about="#mwt15" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-2"}}"><a href="#cite_note-2" id="mwGA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwGQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGg">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGw">]</span></span></a></sup> MOIL operates 11 mines in adjoining districts of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra" title="Maharashtra" id="mwHA">Maharashtra</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh" title="Madhya Pradesh" id="mwHQ">Madhya Pradesh</a>. It has been ranked #486 among the 500 top companies in India and 9th in the mines and metals sector of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_India_500" title="Fortune India 500" id="mwHg">Fortune India 500</a> list for 2011.<sup about="#mwt18" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-3"}}"><a href="#cite_note-3" id="mwHw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwIA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIQ">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwIw">In December 2010, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India" title="Government of India" id="mwJA">Government of India</a> divested about 20% of its equity through an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering" title="Initial public offering" id="mwJQ">IPO</a>. Of the 20%, the Indian Government divested 10%, and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Maharashtra" title="Government of Maharashtra" id="mwJg">Government of Maharashtra</a> and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh" title="Government of Madhya Pradesh" id="mwJw">Government of Madhya Pradesh</a> each divested 5% of the total equity.<sup about="#mwt21" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"}}"><a href="#cite_note-4" id="mwKA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwKQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKg">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt24" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-5"}}"><a href="#cite_note-5" id="mwLA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwLQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwLg">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwLw">]</span></span></a></sup> The central government holds 54% and the two state governments hold about 11% shares in MOIL.<sup about="#mwt27" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}"><a href="#cite_note-6" id="mwMA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwMQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMg">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMw">]</span></span></a></sup> and the public holds about 35% shares.</p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwNA" data-mw="{"autoGenerated":true}"></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwNQ" aria-labelledby="History"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="History">History</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=MOIL&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: History"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwNg">MOIL was originally set up as "Central Province Prospecting Syndicate" in the year 1896 in the region of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra" title="Maharashtra" id="mwNw">Maharashtra</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh" title="Madhya Pradesh" id="mwOA">Madhya Pradesh</a>. It was later renamed as "Central Provinces Manganese Ore Company Limited (CPMO)" in 1935. In 1962, the Government of India took over the mining activities from CPMO. Then, Manganese Ore (India) Limited was formed with 51% stake held between the Government of India and the Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh State governments. The other 49% was retained with CPMO.
In 1977, the balance of 49% was acquired from CPMO, and MOIL became a 100% state-owned enterprise.<sup about="#mwt28" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-pim_7-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"pim"}}"><a href="#cite_note-pim-7" id="mwOQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwOg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOw">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt31" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}"><a href="#cite_note-8" id="mwPQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwPg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPw">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwQQ" aria-labelledby="Mines"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Mines">Mines</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=MOIL&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Mines"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwQg">Eight of MOIL's eleven mines are underground mines (Kandri, Munsar, Beldongri, Gumgaon, Chikla, Balaghat, and Ukwa mines) and three are opencast mines (Dongri Buzurg, Sitapatore, and Tirodi).<sup about="#mwt32" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-redherr_1-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"redherr"}}"><a href="#cite_note-redherr-1" id="mwQw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwRA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRQ">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRg">]</span></span></a></sup> Its Balaghat mine is the largest of the 11 mines and the deepest at 383 metres.<sup about="#mwt35" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-pim_7-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"pim"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-pim-7"}}"><a href="#cite_note-pim-7" id="mwRw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwSA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSQ">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
